name: Canton
executive_summary: Canton Network's public network and Canton Coin went live in July 2024, not yet two years old at the time of this scoring, built specifically for institutional finance with transaction-level privacy built into the protocol rather than bolted on. Real-World Utility and Privacy & Confidentiality are its strongest categories, both scoring 88, reflecting $344 billion in represented asset value moving across the network. The TradFi score is held to 65, eleven points below its underlying 76, because the network hasn't yet secured the kind of formal U.S. regulatory recognition, such as a commodity classification, ETF, or futures listing, that would unlock the rest of that score, even though its AI score of 75 already reads as more agent-ready than institution-ready today.

binding_cap.short_note: Capped by Regulatory Clarity Partial -- not on the March 2026 SEC-CFTC digital commodities list, no CME futures, no ETF.

key_findings: All three TradFi gates sit at Partial.
An 11-point gate-driven reduction from raw 76.00 to published 65 -- the Regulatory Clarity cap is doing real work here.
Real-World Utility (88) reflects $344.83B in represented asset value via RWA.xyz, CC's strongest category alongside privacy.

Privacy & Confidentiality (88) -- sub-transaction privacy is a protocol-level property, with each participant seeing only the parts of a transaction they are party to. Required disclosure: this protects Daml application transactions; Canton Coin balances and transaction history are themselves publicly visible via the network's scan service.

binding_cap.short_note: Capped by Deterministic Finality Partial -- a tight 1.5-point bind.

key_findings: AI score (75) sits above TradFi score (65), a negative divergence.
Privacy & Confidentiality (95) is CC's strongest AI category by a wide margin.
Same chain, two different binding gates on two axes -- Regulatory Clarity on TradFi, Deterministic Finality on AI.

watch_items: Zenith (EVM/SVM execution layer) was testnet-only at AI scoring -- mainnet would be a reality-changed re-credit candidate for Agent Tooling, Standards & Interoperability, and Execution Layer.

A US commodity classification, ETF, or CME futures listing would lift the TradFi Regulatory Clarity cap. The cap is currently cutting 11 points, so this is the single highest-impact pending event for this chain's TradFi score.
